transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I’m Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I… I guess I’m here because there’s been this situation with the ensemble. For almost two years now, since a commission, I’ve felt pretty certain that a few people have been using things like schedule changes, where people sit, little comments in rehearsals… to sort of quietly undermine my work.

They’ve shown me emails or notes that are supposed to explain it, but it doesn’t really change what I’m seeing.
Can you tell me more about why you believe these people are trying to undermine your work? Have you noticed any specific actions that make you feel this way, or is it more of a feeling?

It’s… not just a feeling. I mean, it started after that commission, and since then there have been these small things.

Schedules getting shifted in ways that make my work harder, where people are placed in rehearsals, comments that sound casual but aren’t really casual. It’s hard to explain without sounding… overly focused on it.

They’ll show me an email or a note that’s supposed to explain why something happened, but I still feel pretty certain there’s more behind it. It’s been almost two years, and I haven’t really been able to shake that.
Have you ever felt certain that these actions were intentionally meant to harm or discredit you, even if others have tried to explain them as normal or routine changes?

Yes. I mean… that’s the part I can’t really shake.

Even when they show me emails or notes saying it was just scheduling or some routine decision, it still feels intentional. After that commission, it seemed like a few people started using those little things—schedule changes, seating, comments in rehearsal—to quietly make my work look worse or make things harder for me.
Has this kind of thing happened to you before in other groups or jobs, or is this the first time you’ve felt like people have been trying to undermine your work in this way?

This is the first time it’s been like this, I think. I mean… I’ve had disagreements in other settings, sure, but not this.

This started after that commission, with this ensemble. Since then I just haven’t been able to shake the sense that a few people are doing these small things on purpose—schedules, seating, comments in rehearsal—even when there’s some email or explanation for it.
Have you ever felt that these actions were part of a coordinated plan or that others were working together in secret against you?

Yes… I think so. I don’t know how organized it is, exactly, but it feels like a few of them are on the same page.

After that commission, the schedule changes, the seating choices, the little comments in rehearsal… it just started feeling too consistent to be random. Even when they show me emails or notes explaining it, I still can’t really believe that’s all it is.
Have you noticed any other changes that others might not notice, like hearing things, seeing things, or having thoughts that feel unusual or hard to explain?

No… not really. I haven’t noticed anything like that.

I mean, I get stuck thinking about what’s been happening, but I’m not hearing or seeing things, if that’s what you mean.
Have you ever felt certain about something happening—like these schedule changes or comments—without any proof or reason to believe it, even though others might not see it the same way?

Yes… I guess that’s the part that’s hard to explain.

I don’t have, like, a document proving it. But after the commission, when the schedule changes kept happening, and the seating, and those little comments in rehearsal… it felt obvious to me that a few people were trying to quietly push me aside or undermine what I was doing.

Even when they show me emails or notes explaining it, I still don’t really believe that’s the whole story.
